problem: Standard Swift run: quick succeeded where old test expected a throw inside a presumed 150ms gate window
sample_identity: swiftpm-testing-helper test runner with ParentExitTests synchronous read/wait work on main thread; sample includes CommandTerminationTests stack
root_cause: Test slept 20ms after scheduling an async termination task and assumed the actor resumed before its 150ms deadline. Task sleep specifies a minimum delay; delayed continuation can observe the correctly reopened gate. A deterministic late-resume experiment reproduces the same incorrect test expectation.
production_change: Synchronous beginTermination closes gate and interrupts registered own children before AppDelegate returns terminateLater; async waitForTermination establishes deadline when waiting starts. prepareForTermination delegates to both phases.

phase_semantics.accepting: New ordinary commands allowed. begin returns true and moves to draining.
phase_semantics.draining: Gate closed synchronously; repeated begin returns false; wait enters waiting.
phase_semantics.waiting: Single bounded wait active; duplicate wait returns timedOut without changing original request; timeout/cancellation returns accepting and preserves active operations.
phase_semantics.sealed: Reader and writer completed; gate remains closed for app exit; begin returns false and duplicate wait returns timedOut.
phase_semantics.unbegun_wait: Returns timedOut and leaves accepting state unchanged.

new_test_observations: Gate rejection happens after synchronous begin and before timeout starts
Blocked quick command creates no child marker, history entry or extra log
Unchanged 150ms wait reports timedOut while escaped writer remains running
After timeout, quick child creates marker and completes; escaped final tail persists after release
Unbegun wait, repeated begin and completed drain sealing have explicit regression coverage
